puzzles.title: Skip to content
puzzles.question: 'Skip to content' on one website, a list of psychology fields on another. Why the same neuron?
puzzles.reveal: It fires on the joints of navigation menus: the 'to' in 'Skip to…', the bars in 'Methods | Statistics | Clinical'. A recipe laid out as 'Jump to Ingredients | Jump to Instructions' lights it up; the same words written as a sentence don't.
puzzles.factor: Token is part of a navigation skip link or delimiter in a structured menu/navigation system, appearing between repeated structural elements

puzzles.question: Summer Olympics, research news. The neuron fires on 'the' and 'a'. Why there?
puzzles.reveal: It fires on the word right after a sentence that opens with 'In' or 'At'. 'In my kitchen…' lights it; 'The copper pots in my kitchen…' doesn't. It's tracking how the sentence began, not what it's about.

puzzles.title: A comma and a line break
puzzles.question: A comma in a health site's footer and a line break in a dictionary. Why do they fire together?
puzzles.reveal: Both sit on the seam where ordinary text turns into reference metadata: a date line, a source, a definition. 'Passed down through generations,⏎Published: March 15…' fires it; the same facts in one sentence don't.
puzzles.factor: Token that ends a sentence or clause immediately before a new line or formatted section begins with standardized information
